requirements.semantic_brief: Screen for candidates whose role experience is Frontend Engineer or equivalent frontend engineering work, with React and JavaScript each independently required. Require at least 3 years of overall employment, not limited to the requested role. Prefer, but do not require, TypeScript, automated testing, and Git. Evidence may be based on resume claims and equivalent role/work descriptions; no personal or non-job-related attributes are considered.

evidence_standards.capability: Frontend developer work: building, implementing, or maintaining user-facing frontend software or interfaces.
evidence_standards.sufficient_evidence: A stated Frontend Engineer or frontend developer role, or source evidence of equivalent frontend development work, supports the criterion.
evidence_standards.equivalence_boundary: Equivalent frontend development work may be described using different titles or narrower frontend responsibilities; adjacent design, backend-only, or general software work alone does not establish the requested role.
evidence_standards.uncertainty_boundary: Absence of a stated role or equivalent work is insufficient evidence. Ambiguous titles without described frontend responsibilities remain uncertain; conflicting role evidence requires resolution.

evidence_standards.capability: React capability.
evidence_standards.sufficient_evidence: An explicit React claim or source work demonstrating use of React establishes presence.
evidence_standards.equivalence_boundary: Different wording or a narrower React implementation may establish the same capability; adjacent JavaScript, frontend, or similarly named technologies alone do not.
evidence_standards.uncertainty_boundary: No React claim or demonstrated React work is absence of evidence, not evidence of inability. Vague or ambiguous framework references remain uncertain; contradictory evidence requires resolution.

evidence_standards.capability: JavaScript capability.
evidence_standards.sufficient_evidence: An explicit JavaScript claim or source work demonstrating JavaScript establishes presence.
evidence_standards.equivalence_boundary: Different wording or a narrower JavaScript implementation may establish the same capability; adjacent frontend work or other programming languages alone do not.
evidence_standards.uncertainty_boundary: No JavaScript claim or demonstrated JavaScript work is absence of evidence, not evidence of inability. Vague language references remain uncertain; contradictory evidence requires resolution.

evidence_standards.capability: At least 3 years of overall employment, counting stated employment across occupations, including internships or employment during study when presented as employment.
evidence_standards.sufficient_evidence: Dated employment evidence whose qualifying intervals total at least 3 years supports the criterion, including qualifying employment across different occupations and stated internships or employment during study.
evidence_standards.equivalence_boundary: Different employment-title wording and non-full-time or study-period employment may count when the source presents the activity as employment; undated activities, isolated projects, or skills lists do not establish employment duration.
evidence_standards.uncertainty_boundary: Missing or incomplete dates prevent confirming the threshold. Overlapping or ambiguous intervals require conservative clarification; evidence totaling less than 3 years does not meet the criterion.

evidence_standards.capability: TypeScript capability.
evidence_standards.sufficient_evidence: An explicit TypeScript claim or source work demonstrating TypeScript establishes presence of the preferred skill.
evidence_standards.equivalence_boundary: Different wording or a narrower TypeScript implementation may establish the same capability; adjacent JavaScript or other typed-language experience alone does not.
evidence_standards.uncertainty_boundary: No TypeScript claim or demonstrated TypeScript work leaves the preference unconfirmed, not disproven. Vague or contradictory evidence remains uncertain.

evidence_standards.capability: Automated testing capability: using automation to execute software tests.
evidence_standards.sufficient_evidence: An explicit automated-testing claim or source work demonstrating automated execution of software tests establishes presence of the preferred skill.
evidence_standards.equivalence_boundary: Different wording or a narrower automated-testing implementation may establish the same capability; manual testing, general quality assurance, or automation unrelated to software tests alone does not.
evidence_standards.uncertainty_boundary: No automated-testing claim or demonstrated work leaves the preference unconfirmed, not disproven. References that do not clarify whether testing was automated remain uncertain; contradictory evidence requires resolution.

evidence_standards.capability: Git capability: using Git for version-control work.
evidence_standards.sufficient_evidence: An explicit Git claim or source work demonstrating use of Git establishes presence of the preferred skill.
evidence_standards.equivalence_boundary: Different wording or a narrower Git implementation may establish the same capability; version-control experience with another system alone does not establish Git capability.
evidence_standards.uncertainty_boundary: No Git claim or demonstrated Git work leaves the preference unconfirmed, not disproven. Generic version-control references without identifying Git remain uncertain; contradictory evidence requires resolution.
